answer: Grades are sealed when submitted and only opened at close, so graders cannot react to or copy each other, which prevents a Sybil cluster from coordinating its votes within a single jury. The key insight is that coordination itself leaks: the more unified a farm is, the more easily its shared style or timing betrays it. This is why the honest majority can be small yet decisive: each vote carries the weight of verifiable work, not just the noise of a large flock. Consider a ledge as the anchor of the cost.
